entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 2</hi> <div eID="gen13545" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13546" type="x-p"/> Now the first inhabitants - This is spoken of those who returned from the Babylonish captivity, and of the time in which they returned; for it is insinuated here that other persons afterwards settled at Jerusalem, though these mentioned here were the first on the return from the captivity. Properly speaking, the divisions mentioned in this verse constituted the whole of the Israelitish people, who were, ever since the days of Joshua, divided into the four following classes: <div eID="gen13546" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13547" type="x-p"/> 1. The priests. <div eID="gen13547" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13548" type="x-p"/> 2. The Levites. <div eID="gen13548" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13549" type="x-p"/> 3. The common people, or simple Israelites. <div eID="gen13549" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13550" type="x-p"/> 4. The Nethinim, or slaves of the temple, the remains of the Gibeonites, who, having deceived Joshua, were condemned to this service <reference osisRef="Jos.9.21">Jos 9:21</reference>, etc. In David's time it is probable that other conquered people were added, as the successors of the Gibeonites were not sufficient to perform all the drudgery of the temple service.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 3</hi> <div eID="gen13550" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13551" type="x-p"/> And in Jerusalem dwelt - Several of the tribes of Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh, took advantage of the proclamation of Cyrus to return to Jerusalem, and so mingled with the Israelites, and those to whom Jerusalem had previously appertained; and this was necessary in order to provide a sufficient population for so large a city.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 4</hi> <div eID="gen13551" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13552" type="x-p"/> Uthai the son of Ammihud - The list here is nearly the same with those found in Ezra and Nehemiah, and contains those who returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel; but the list in Nehemiah is more ample, probably because it contains those who came afterwards. The object of the sacred writer here was to give the list of those who came first. Now the first inhabitants, etc.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 11</hi> <div eID="gen13552" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13553" type="x-p"/> The ruler of the house of God - The high priest at this time was Jeshua the son of Jozadak, (<reference osisRef="Ezr.3.8">Ezr 3:8</reference>), and Seraiah, (<reference osisRef="Neh.11.11">Neh 11:11</reference>), called here Azariah, was the ruler of the house; the person next in authority to the high priest, and who probably had the guard of the temple and command of the priests, Levites, etc. It is likely that the person here was the same as is called the second priest, <reference osisRef="2Kgs.25.18">2Kgs 25:18</reference> (note), who was the sagan or high priest's deputy. See the note there.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 35</hi> <div eID="gen13558" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13559" type="x-p"/> Whose wife's name was Maachah - Here our translators have departed from the original, for the word is אחתו achotho, his Sister; but the Vulgate, Septuagint, Syriac, Arabic, and Chaldee, have Wife; to which may be added <reference osisRef="1Chr.8.29">1Chr 8:29</reference>, the parallel place. Almost all the early editions, as well as the MS. editions, have the same reading. Of all the Polyglots the Complutensian alone has אשתו ishto, his Wife. His wife is the reading also of Vatablus's Polyglot, but in the margin he observes that other copies have his sister. There is most certainly a fault somewhere, for Maachah could not be both the sister and wife of Jehiel. Whether, therefore, <reference osisRef="1Chr.8.29">1Chr 8:29</reference> has been altered from this, or this altered from that, who can tell? A single letter makes the whole difference: if the word be written with ח cheth, it is Sister; if with ש shin, it is Wife. The latter is most probably the true reading. It is so in three very ancient MSS. in my own possession.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 41</hi> <div eID="gen13559" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13560" type="x-p"/> And Ahaz - This is added by our translators from <reference osisRef="1Chr.8.35">1Chr 8:35</reference>, but such liberties should only be taken in a note; for although the words are now sufficiently distinguished from the text by being printed in Italics, yet it is too much to expect that every editor of a Bible will attend to such distinctions, and in process of time the words will be found incorporated with the text. <reference osisRef="1Chr.9.35">1Chr 9:35</reference>, and the following verses, are a repetition of what we find in <reference osisRef="1Chr.8.29-1Chr.8.38">1Chr 8:29-38</reference> (note), where see the notes.  <chapter eID="1Chr.9"/> <div eID="gen13560" type="x-p"/>
